statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH; Tail is at the top of the watch band as the FOMC press-conference phase remains unresolved.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; the remaining near-term checkpoint is the 18:30 UTC press conference and any delayed cross-asset second leg.
headline: Fed hikes 25 bp; Tail remains WATCH pending price-path confirmation
body: The Fed raised the target range to 3.75%-4.00%, and 16 of 18 policymakers projected at least one more 2026 hike. Fresh supplementary latest-session breadth showed 6/8 megacaps and 6/7 semiconductors positive, but immediate post-decision NQ retracement/extension structure is not independently verified.

lookbackSummary: Over the prior 24 clock hours, Tail moved from WATCH late September 15 to low overnight, briefly returned to WATCH around September 16 U.S. data and the cash session, then stood at 19% before the FOMC decision. Stress remained 99-100%.
outlookSummary: The immediate residual risk is the 18:30 UTC FOMC press conference and a possible delayed rates/equity second leg into the close. Tail should decay if price discovery is two-way and retracements remain meaningful. The next U.S. data cluster is 12:30 UTC on September 17.

forecast.analysis: The cash-close transition can transmit a delayed FOMC second leg. Tail is 23% WATCH unless the policy move keeps extending with failed retracements; a two-way close would support faster risk decay.

Post-close trade should begin separating the policy impulse from ordinary event volatility. Tail is 20% WATCH while delayed repricing remains possible; stabilization across rates and equity futures would favor normalization.
If futures trade becomes two-way and cross-assets stabilize, Tail falls to 19% low. Stress remains extreme because the first post-FOMC handoff can still carry residual repricing.
Continued stabilization would support 18% low Tail. A renewed rates-led extension with shallow pullbacks would interrupt the expected post-event decay.
The Asia handoff should test whether the FOMC impulse is reinforced or retraced. Without sustained directional efficiency, Tail remains 18% low while Stress continues to ease.
A balanced early-Asia session would keep Tail at 17% low. A fresh rates or geopolitical discontinuity would be the main path back toward WATCH.
Two-way overnight trade would support 17% low Tail. Persistent holding near an extreme with repeated failed retracements would invalidate the normalization path.
Late-Asia conditions are expected to remain normalized if no delayed policy leg emerges. Tail stays 17% low unless directional efficiency strengthens materially.
The pre-Europe hour carries low Tail under a stable overnight baseline. A synchronized move in yields, semiconductors and index futures would be the main escalation signal.
Europe's approach should keep Tail at 17% low if overnight retracements remain healthy. A clean break with poor pullback quality would challenge the baseline.
The Europe handoff can reprice the prior FOMC message, but Tail remains 17% low unless that repricing becomes persistent and one-way.
European trading should provide a second test of overnight balance. Tail stays 17% low if moves continue to retrace rather than extend repeatedly.
A stable European morning keeps Tail low. Renewed energy or rates pressure would raise Stress first and Tail only if index price action also turns persistently directional.
As U.S. participation increases, Tail edges to 18% low. The relevant condition is whether overnight levels hold with normal retracement or begin showing failed pullbacks.
The U.S. premarket transition lifts uncertainty modestly but leaves Tail at 18% low. Cross-asset alignment would matter more than headline volatility alone.
Ahead of the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster, Tail is 19% low and Stress rises. The releases are checkpoints rather than automatic Tail evidence.
drivers: Housing, claims and Philadelphia Fed cluster

forecast.analysis: Housing starts, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey arrive at 12:30 UTC. Tail is 20% WATCH conditionally; only persistent post-release extension or failed retracements would justify higher bands.
The 13:30 UTC cash open follows the data cluster. Tail is 21% WATCH conditionally because opening-auction continuation can amplify a move; healthy pullbacks would argue for rapid decay.
The first post-open hour should reveal whether the data/opening move is persistent or mean-reverting. Tail is 20% WATCH pending that conditional structure.
If the U.S. morning develops two-way structure, Tail returns to 19% low. Persistent session-extreme holding would be the main reason for a higher path.
Mid-session conditions favor 18% low Tail if volatility continues to retrace. A new rates or geopolitical impulse could interrupt the normalization path.
By late morning, Tail remains 18% low under a two-way baseline. Repeated failed pullbacks would be the clearest invalidation of that baseline.

forecastDetail.comment: Fed hike and projections are known; post-decision NQ structure is not yet independently verified, so Tail remains 24% WATCH into the press conference.
Press-conference and power-hour overlap is the main conditional second-leg checkpoint; 24% WATCH assumes no confirmed mean-reversion failure yet.
Cash-close repricing remains conditional; Tail is 23% WATCH unless extension persists with failed retracements.
Post-close digestion should separate policy impulse from ordinary volatility; Tail is 20% WATCH while delayed repricing remains possible.
If two-way futures trade and cross-assets stabilize, Tail falls to 19% low while residual policy Stress stays high.
Continued stabilization supports 18% low Tail; renewed rates-led extension with shallow pullbacks would interrupt the decay.
